authentication.method: possession-based one-use invitation, with a separate recipient return capability

verification.typeScript: passed in the final production build

observedContracts: Concurrent repeated issuance produces one original link and deadline.
Current inviter membership and session authority are checked around delayed database work.
Independent competing holders produce at most one recipient grant.
Exact browser, intent and payload retries return the original accepted session.
Fresh return capability possession restores the exact original session and fixed expiry.
An unrelated active or ended credential must be explicitly set aside before entry.
Revocation preserves original grant, commitments and financial history while ending access.
A sponsor has its own donor actor and can accept only its own unpaid grant or pledge choices.
No session token is returned as JSON; public HTML, events and snapshots exclude private invitation data.
Invitation pages and APIs are private and non-cacheable, with no-referrer headers.
All template organizers can navigate to invitations; non-organizer template views omit that action.
retainedFailures: The first adversarial run found five stale-context or expiry-after-lock defects; the corrected expanded fifteen-case run passes without weakened assertions.
The first draft test harness compared JSON property insertion order; it was corrected to compare normalized saved representation while preserving contract-value assertions.
The first build reached successful compilation but rejected in-progress test callback return types; explicit never-returning test helpers resolved that TypeScript error.
The first HTTP harness expected GET 404 from POST-only disabled fixture routes; correct behavior is GET 405 and disabled POST 404.
Node fetch ignored a supplied Host header in a negative HTTP test; a raw HTTP request verified actual mismatched-host rejection. The earlier valid request and its records were retained.
